deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 2% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.2% = 10-year Treasury 5.2% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 250% last year; 105%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 87% (3 years ago -10%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $87 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 61% (3 years ago -13%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $134.0B — about 1.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $13.0B, up from $169M a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 105%/yr over 3 years and 37%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 75% vs a 5-year range of -41–75% (median 24%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.3B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($650M buybacks + $610M dividends) = 0.2% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

note.headline: Micron falls 7.62% to 719.02 on no news, breaks below 200-day average

summary.thesis: Micron is still a grade-A, cash-rich business, but the price is now in a downtrend and sits just above the 703.86 value that assumes zero cash-flow growth.
summary.decision: Hold long-term and add only on the 643.61–658.4 support zone; no swing trade until that support holds or the price recovers 745.16.
summary.act_at: Add at 658.4; trim above 833.11; reconsider on a close below 643.61

note.happening: MU closed at 719.02, down 7.62% in a day from 778.31, with no news reported since the last note. That drop took the price below the 200-day average of 766.94 and through the old 730–745 support area, which now acts as resistance at 730.37–745.16. The next earnings report is due 2026-12-23.
note.business: Nothing in DATA changes the business today. The drop came with no news, so it is a sentiment and trend move, not a change in demand, margins or cash. The latest filed numbers are still exceptional. Trailing revenue is 133.2B, up from 37.4B. Quarterly revenue grew 345.03% from a year earlier, up from 196.29% two quarters ago. The operating margin is 74.59%, and free cash flow is 59.0B. The balance sheet is safe: 40.6B of net cash, against only 2.8B of debt. The real risk is the margin, not the balance sheet. The operating margin was 26.14% a year earlier and now sits at the top of its 5-year range (-41% to 75%). Memory chip prices tend to move in cycles (general knowledge), and the filings flag that peaks like this usually fade. On governance, insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set plans. That is a sentiment signal, not a business change. What is at risk is how long the profits stay this high. The cash pile and the company's survival are not at risk.

worth.text: No standard discounted cash flow (DCF) value is available. A DCF values a company on its future cash, but free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a jump like that can't be projected forward. Two other angles help instead. First, what the price implies: the market prices in starting cash-flow growth of only 0.5%, and the value with zero growth is 703.86. So at 719.02, the price assumes today's cash flow roughly holds and does not grow. Second, multiples look cheap: the trailing P/E (price over the last year's earnings) is 9.7, and price/sales is 6.1 against a peer median of 8.2. The whole gap between methods comes from one question: are today's peak margins normal or temporary? If the operating margin falls to 37%, the value is 779.6, and that figure assumes 20% starting growth. If margins return to the historical middle, the own-history mid of 490.66 is the better guide.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near today's 59.0B rather than shrinking sharply as the 74.59% operating margin fades from its 5-year peak.

bull: The trailing P/E is 9.7 and price/sales is 6.1, below the peer median of 8.2, so the stock is cheap against similar companies on today's earnings.
Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly revenue grew 345.03% year on year, against 196.29% two quarters ago, and 30.81% quarter on quarter.
There is 40.6B of net cash and 59.0B of trailing free cash flow, a 44.27% free cash flow margin, so the balance sheet can absorb a downturn.
bear: The operating margin of 74.59% is at the top of its 5-year range, up from 26.14% a year earlier, and the filings note that peaks like this usually fade.
The trend is down: the price is below the 20-day (828.71), 50-day (937.74) and 200-day (766.94) averages, and the committee call is Reduce.

longterm.why: At 719.02, the price is near the bottom of the 703.86–833.11 fair range, and the business is unchanged. The downtrend argues against adding before the price tests support at 658.4.

swing.why: The price is in a downtrend, just under resistance at 730.37–745.16, which is less than one 59.18 ATR (average daily range) away, so the upside to resistance is too small for the risk. Enter only if the 643.61–658.4 support holds on a test, or on a close back above 745.16.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-23 report falls inside the 2027-01-15 options expiry, which prices a 21.9% move, and implied volatility of 74.0 is below the recent realized 106.4, so swings may run larger than options price. That makes new positions before the report an event risk, and the report's margin figure will set the next move.

change_mind: A close below 643.61, the bottom of the support zone, would move the long-term call from hold to wait and point toward the 435.76–471.0 support zone.
If the 2026-12-23 report shows the operating margin falling toward 37%, where the value is 779.6 with 20% starting growth, the high end of the range would need to come down from 833.11.
A close back above 745.16, plus the price recovering the 766.94 200-day average, would undo the breakdown and support a swing entry.
